explanation: Relation: A is a mild degree and B the extreme degree of the same quality (heat; costliness). Tepid is slightly warm and searing extremely hot; pricey is somewhat expensive and exorbitant outrageously expensive.

distractor_rationales.irked is to petrified: Mild to extreme, but on two different scales (annoyance vs. fear), so not one quality intensified.
distractor_rationales.frosty is to sweltering: Opposite ends of the temperature scale, not a milder and stronger form of one quality.
distractor_rationales.antiquated is to outmoded: Near-synonyms of equal strength; no intensification.
distractor_rationales.grueling is to spent: Cause and effect: a grueling task leaves a person spent.

explanation: Relation: A is a mild form and B a forceful form of the same action (scolding; pressuring). To chide is to scold mildly and to berate is to scold harshly; to urge is to press gently and to coerce is to press by force.

distractor_rationales.rebuke is to reprimand: Two verbs of roughly equal force for scolding; no mild-to-strong step.
distractor_rationales.goad is to erupt: Cause and response: goading someone may make them erupt.
distractor_rationales.commend is to denounce: Opposites (praise vs. condemn), not two strengths of one act.
distractor_rationales.inquire is to reply: Sequence: an inquiry is followed by a reply.

explanation: Relation: A is a moderate degree and B an intense degree of the same feeling. Esteem is respect and reverence is deep, awed respect; satisfaction is contentment and rapture is overwhelming delight.

distractor_rationales.suspicion is to exultation: Two unrelated feelings; not one feeling intensified.
distractor_rationales.insolence is to indignation: Cause and effect: insolence provokes indignation.

explanation: Relation: A is a reasonable degree of a trait and B an excessive degree of the same trait. An assertive person states views firmly, a domineering one overrides others; a selective person chooses carefully, a finicky one is excessively hard to please.

distractor_rationales.subdued is to exuberant: Opposites, not two degrees of one trait.
distractor_rationales.sedentary is to flabby: Cause and effect: a sedentary life can make one flabby.

explanation: Relation: A is a slight degree and B an extreme degree of the same action (striking; burning). To graze is to strike lightly and to wallop is to strike very hard; to singe is to burn slightly and to incinerate is to burn completely.

distractor_rationales.chafe is to redden: Cause and effect: chafing makes skin redden.

explanation: Relation: A is a slight degree and B the fullest degree of the same thing (quarrel; command of a language). A tiff is a minor quarrel and a vendetta a prolonged, bitter feud; a smattering is a slight knowledge of a language and fluency full command of it.

distractor_rationales.glint is to tempest: Unrelated things; not one thing in two degrees.
distractor_rationales.gaffe is to mortification: Cause and effect: a gaffe causes mortification.

explanation: Relation: A is a mild degree and B an extreme degree of the same mood. Glum is mildly gloomy and despondent utterly without hope; peeved is mildly annoyed and livid furiously angry.

distractor_rationales.irate is to incensed: Near-synonyms, both already very angry; no mild-to-extreme step.
distractor_rationales.slighted is to vengeful: Cause and effect: feeling slighted can make one vengeful.

explanation: Relation: A is a mild form and B an extreme form of the same action. To sniffle is to cry quietly and to bawl is to cry loudly and hard; to disappoint is to let someone down mildly and to devastate is to crush them.

distractor_rationales.frighten is to flinch: Cause and response: being frightened makes one flinch.
distractor_rationales.exalt is to debase: Opposites (raise up vs. lower in esteem).

explanation: Relation: something that is A is by definition without B. An artless person has no guile; insipid food has no flavor.

distractor_rationales.ardent is to zest: An ardent person is FULL of zest: possession, the reverse of lacking.
distractor_rationales.harrowing is to distress: A harrowing event CAUSES distress in others; it does not lack it.
distractor_rationales.acquisitive is to property: An acquisitive person is eager to GAIN property; desire, not absence.

explanation: Relation: someone who is A is by definition without B. A callow youth lacks maturity; an insolvent business lacks the funds to pay its debts.

distractor_rationales.precocious is to aptitude: A precocious child shows aptitude early: possession, not absence.
distractor_rationales.avid is to novelty: An avid person is eager FOR something; desire, not absence.

explanation: Relation: something that is A is by definition without B. Amorphous means without definite form; inert means without motion or activity.

distractor_rationales.deafening is to hearing: A deafening noise DESTROYS others’ hearing; it is not itself without hearing.
distractor_rationales.redundant is to repetition: Something redundant is characterized BY needless repetition.
distractor_rationales.tangible is to touch: Something tangible CAN be perceived by touch: capability, not absence.

explanation: Relation: someone who is A is by definition without B. A tactless person lacks discretion; an intrepid person feels no fright.

distractor_rationales.jovial is to mirth: A jovial person is FULL of mirth.
distractor_rationales.daring is to audacity: A daring person HAS audacity; possession, though on the same courage axis as the key.

explanation: Relation: someone who is A is by definition without B. An unscrupulous person has no moral principles; an uncouth person has no refinement.

distractor_rationales.covetous is to belongings: A covetous person DESIRES others’ belongings.

explanation: Relation: something that is A is by definition without B. Unkempt hair has had no grooming; a groundless accusation has no basis.

distractor_rationales.substantiated is to proof: A substantiated claim HAS proof, the reverse of the key.
distractor_rationales.speculative is to conjecture: A speculative idea CONSISTS of conjecture; it is made of it, not without it.

explanation: Relation: someone or something that is A is by definition without B. A pallid face lacks color; a callous person lacks sympathy.

distractor_rationales.empathetic is to understanding: An empathetic person HAS understanding of others.
distractor_rationales.vulnerable is to exploitation: Someone vulnerable is OPEN to exploitation.

explanation: Relation: someone who is A is by definition without B. A dispirited team has lost its morale; an unwitting accomplice acts without awareness.

distractor_rationales.studious is to scholarship: A studious person is DEVOTED to scholarship.
distractor_rationales.premeditated is to intent: A premeditated act is done WITH prior intent, the reverse of the key.

explanation: Relation: a person called A is characteristically B. A curmudgeon is by nature grouchy; a busybody is by nature meddlesome.

distractor_rationales.follower is to charismatic: A follower is drawn to a charismatic LEADER; the adjective describes someone else.
distractor_rationales.bully is to defenseless: A bully preys on defenseless VICTIMS; the adjective describes the target.
distractor_rationales.worrywart is to carefree: A worrywart is the OPPOSITE of carefree.
distractor_rationales.pioneer is to uncharted: A pioneer explores uncharted TERRITORY; the adjective describes the place.

explanation: Relation: a person called A is characteristically B. A stoic is by nature impassive; a maverick is by nature independent.

distractor_rationales.underdog is to favored: An underdog is precisely NOT favored.
distractor_rationales.mentor is to unproven: A mentor guides someone unproven; the adjective describes the PROTEGE.
distractor_rationales.scapegoat is to blameworthy: A scapegoat is blamed but is characteristically NOT blameworthy.
distractor_rationales.fugitive is to captured: A fugitive is by definition NOT captured.

explanation: Relation: a person called A is characteristically B. A renegade is by nature disloyal; a snob is by nature condescending.

distractor_rationales.loner is to convivial: A loner is the OPPOSITE of convivial.
distractor_rationales.censor is to obscene: A censor suppresses obscene MATERIAL; the adjective describes the target.
distractor_rationales.arbiter is to contested: An arbiter settles contested MATTERS; the adjective describes what is judged.
distractor_rationales.detractor is to laudatory: A detractor is the OPPOSITE of laudatory.

explanation: Relation: a person called A is characteristically B. A fatalist is by outlook passive before events; a perfectionist is by nature exacting.

distractor_rationales.hothead is to unflappable: A hothead is the OPPOSITE of unflappable.
distractor_rationales.therapist is to distraught: A therapist treats distraught CLIENTS; the adjective describes them.
distractor_rationales.usurper is to rightful: A usurper is precisely NOT the rightful ruler.
distractor_rationales.archivist is to historical: An archivist keeps historical RECORDS; the adjective describes the material.

explanation: Relation: a person called A is characteristically B. An introvert is by nature reticent; a pushover is by nature compliant.

distractor_rationales.malcontent is to gratified: A malcontent is the OPPOSITE of gratified.
distractor_rationales.insider is to uninformed: An insider is the OPPOSITE of uninformed.
distractor_rationales.rescuer is to stranded: A rescuer saves stranded PEOPLE; the adjective describes them.
distractor_rationales.arsonist is to flammable: An arsonist sets flammable THINGS alight; the adjective describes the material.

explanation: Relation: a person called A is characteristically B. A visionary is by nature farsighted; a dupe is by nature unsuspecting.

distractor_rationales.swindler is to unwary: A swindler preys on unwary VICTIMS; the adjective describes the target, not the swindler.
distractor_rationales.dynamo is to indolent: A dynamo is the OPPOSITE of indolent.
distractor_rationales.celebrity is to anonymous: A celebrity is the OPPOSITE of anonymous.

explanation: Relation: a person called A is characteristically B. An extrovert is by nature outgoing; an egotist is by nature conceited.

distractor_rationales.altruist is to mercenary: An altruist is the OPPOSITE of mercenary.
distractor_rationales.reformer is to corrupt: A reformer targets corrupt INSTITUTIONS; the adjective describes them.
distractor_rationales.appraiser is to antique: An appraiser values antique OBJECTS; the adjective describes the goods.
distractor_rationales.neophyte is to seasoned: A neophyte is the OPPOSITE of seasoned.

explanation: Relation: a person called A is characteristically B. A partisan is by nature biased; a purist is by nature unbending about standards.

distractor_rationales.centrist is to extreme: A centrist is the OPPOSITE of extreme.
distractor_rationales.heretic is to orthodox: A heretic is the OPPOSITE of orthodox.

explanation: Relation: a person called A is characteristically B. A connoisseur is by nature discerning; a skinflint is by nature tightfisted.

distractor_rationales.daydreamer is to grounded: A daydreamer is the OPPOSITE of grounded.
distractor_rationales.pickpocket is to inattentive: A pickpocket preys on inattentive VICTIMS; the adjective describes the target.
distractor_rationales.warden is to incarcerated: A warden oversees incarcerated PRISONERS; the adjective describes them.
distractor_rationales.trailblazer is to imitative: A trailblazer is the OPPOSITE of imitative.

explanation: Relation: to A is to B in a particular manner. To lope is to run with long, easy strides; to smirk is to smile in a smug manner.

distractor_rationales.clench is to slacken: Opposite actions (tighten vs. loosen a grip).
distractor_rationales.beckon is to approach: Cause and response: beckoning someone makes them approach.

explanation: Relation: to A is to B in a particular manner. To pilfer is to steal in small amounts; to hurl is to throw with great force.

distractor_rationales.foretell is to prophesy: Synonyms; neither is a particular way of doing the other.
distractor_rationales.hunt is to catch: Purpose and result: one hunts in order to catch.
distractor_rationales.evict is to vacate: Cause and effect: evicting a tenant forces them to vacate.

explanation: Relation: to A is to B in a particular manner. To gobble is to eat quickly and greedily; to glower is to look angrily.

distractor_rationales.coil is to lunge: Sequence: a snake coils, then lunges.
distractor_rationales.sadden is to sigh: Cause and response: being saddened makes one sigh.
distractor_rationales.incubate is to hatch: Sequence: eggs are incubated, then hatch.

explanation: Relation: to A is to B in a particular manner. To sob is to cry with convulsive gasps; to jostle is to push roughly against others.

distractor_rationales.hug is to embrace: Synonyms; neither is a particular way of doing the other.
distractor_rationales.bestow is to receive: Reciprocal actions by two different parties.
distractor_rationales.plead is to relent: Cause and response: pleading may make someone relent.

explanation: Relation: to A is to B in a particular manner. To snicker is to laugh in a sly, half-suppressed way; to slouch is to stand with a drooping posture.

distractor_rationales.totter is to topple: Sequence: what totters may then topple.
distractor_rationales.lull is to doze: Cause and effect: being lulled makes one doze.
distractor_rationales.apply is to enroll: Sequence: one applies and then enrolls.

explanation: Relation: to A is to B in a particular manner. To quaff is to drink heartily; to drawl is to speak slowly with drawn-out vowels.

distractor_rationales.binge is to bloat: Cause and effect: bingeing leaves one bloated.
distractor_rationales.nominate is to elect: Sequence: a candidate is nominated, then elected.

explanation: Relation: to A is to B in a particular manner. To cower is to crouch in fear; to yank is to pull suddenly and hard.

distractor_rationales.mock is to retort: Cause and response: being mocked prompts a retort.
distractor_rationales.sign is to ratify: Sequence: a treaty is signed, then ratified.

explanation: Relation: to A is to B in a particular manner. To stomp is to tread heavily; to swat is to strike with a quick, flat blow.

distractor_rationales.entice is to succumb: Cause and response: being enticed may make one succumb.
distractor_rationales.stalk is to pounce: Sequence: a predator stalks, then pounces.

explanation: Relation: to A is to B in a particular manner. To clutch is to grasp tightly and eagerly; to jab is to poke quickly and sharply.

distractor_rationales.jolt is to awaken: Cause and effect: a jolt may awaken a sleeper.
distractor_rationales.enlist is to deploy: Sequence: a soldier enlists, then is deployed.

explanation: Relation: a person who is A rejects or avoids B on principle. A pacifist refuses combat on principle; a teetotaler refuses liquor on principle.

distractor_rationales.insomniac is to slumber: An insomniac LACKS slumber against his will; not a principled refusal.
distractor_rationales.hedonist is to pleasure: A hedonist SEEKS pleasure, the reverse of rejecting it.
distractor_rationales.hypochondriac is to disease: A hypochondriac FEARS and imagines disease; anxiety, not principle.
distractor_rationales.exile is to homeland: An exile is BANISHED from a homeland by others, not by choice.

explanation: Relation: a person who is A rejects or avoids B on principle. A vegetarian refuses meat on principle; an isolationist refuses foreign alliances on principle.

distractor_rationales.vagrant is to lodging: A vagrant LACKS lodging; circumstance, not principle.
distractor_rationales.castaway is to civilization: A castaway is CUT OFF from civilization by accident.

explanation: Relation: a person who is A rejects or opposes B on principle. An ascetic renounces luxury on principle; an abolitionist rejects slavery on principle.

distractor_rationales.widower is to wife: A widower has LOST his wife; loss, not rejection.

explanation: Relation: a person who is A rejects or avoids B on principle. A minimalist rejects clutter on principle; a vegan refuses dairy on principle.

distractor_rationales.addict is to narcotics: An addict DEPENDS on narcotics, the reverse of avoiding them.
distractor_rationales.squatter is to premises: A squatter OCCUPIES premises without right.

explanation: Relation: a person who is A rejects B on principle. A puritan rejects frivolity on principle; an atheist rejects belief in any deity on principle.

distractor_rationales.worshiper is to idol: A worshiper ADORES an idol, the reverse of rejecting it.
distractor_rationales.captive is to autonomy: A captive LACKS autonomy by force, not by principle.

explanation: Relation: a person who is A rejects B on principle. An anarchist rejects hierarchy on principle; a freethinker rejects dogma on principle.

distractor_rationales.layman is to credentials: A layman LACKS professional credentials; not a principled refusal.

explanation: Relation: a person who is A rejects B on principle. A conscientious objector refuses conscription on principle; an egalitarian rejects special privilege on principle.

distractor_rationales.speculator is to windfall: A speculator HOPES FOR a windfall.
distractor_rationales.debtor is to solvency: A debtor LACKS solvency; circumstance, not principle.
distractor_rationales.martyr is to persecution: A martyr SUFFERS persecution; the principle is the martyr’s cause, not a rejection of persecution.

explanation: Relation: a person who is A rejects B on principle. An iconoclast attacks cherished tradition on principle; a rationalist rejects superstition on principle.

distractor_rationales.preservationist is to landmarks: A preservationist PROTECTS landmarks, the reverse of rejecting them.
distractor_rationales.outsider is to membership: An outsider LACKS membership; not a principled refusal.

explanation: Relation: A is a false form of B, put forward in place of the real one. A pretext is a false reason given to hide the real one; an alias is a false name used to hide the real one.

distractor_rationales.paraphrase is to quotation: A paraphrase is an honest RESTATEMENT of a quotation, not a false one.
distractor_rationales.symptom is to malady: A symptom is a SIGN of a malady.
distractor_rationales.prototype is to product: A prototype is an EARLY genuine version of a product.
distractor_rationales.motive is to crime: A motive is the REAL reason behind a crime.

explanation: Relation: A is a pretended show of B, not the real thing. Bravado is a showy pretense of nerve; a feint is a pretended attack meant to mislead.

distractor_rationales.fortitude is to adversity: Fortitude is genuine strength IN THE FACE OF adversity.
distractor_rationales.onslaught is to assault: An onslaught is an especially FIERCE assault: degree, not pretense.
distractor_rationales.retaliation is to aggression: Retaliation is a RESPONSE to aggression.

explanation: Relation: A is a false, pretended form of B. Quackery is fraudulent healing; hypocrisy is a pretense of morality one does not have.

distractor_rationales.cruelty is to compassion: Cruelty is the ABSENCE or opposite of compassion, not a pretense of it.
distractor_rationales.concern is to paranoia: Paranoia is an EXTREME degree of concern.

explanation: Relation: A is a merely outward, insincere show of B. A veneer of sophistication is a thin surface show of it; lip service is an insincere show of commitment.

distractor_rationales.oath is to fidelity: An oath is a sincere PLEDGE of fidelity.
distractor_rationales.lapse is to attention: A lapse is a momentary FAILURE of attention.
distractor_rationales.inclination is to compulsion: A compulsion is an irresistibly STRONG inclination: degree.
distractor_rationales.nuance is to distinction: A nuance is a SUBTLE distinction: degree.

explanation: Relation: A is a false or imitation form of B that lacks its real substance. A travesty of justice is a false mockery of it; a placebo is an imitation medication with no active ingredient.

distractor_rationales.overdose is to dosage: An overdose is an EXCESSIVE dosage: degree.

explanation: Relation: A is a merely nominal form of B, having its name but not its substance. Tokenism is integration in name only; a figurehead is a leader in name only, without real power.

distractor_rationales.deputy is to official: A deputy is a genuine SUBORDINATE of an official.
distractor_rationales.understudy is to lead: An understudy is a real STAND-IN for a lead actor.
distractor_rationales.proxy is to shareholder: A proxy genuinely ACTS FOR a shareholder with real authority.

explanation: Relation: A is a false appearance of B. A mirage is a false appearance of an oasis; pseudoscience is a false appearance of science.

distractor_rationales.etiquette is to decorum: Etiquette is the set of RULES of decorum; both genuine.
distractor_rationales.ambivalence is to resolve: Ambivalence is the ABSENCE of resolve.

explanation: Relation: someone who is A makes an insincere, superficial show of being B. A glib speaker seems articulate but is shallow and insincere; a sanctimonious person makes a hypocritical show of being righteous.

distractor_rationales.plucky is to foolhardy: Foolhardy is an EXCESSIVE degree of plucky.
distractor_rationales.victorious is to jubilant: Cause and effect: being victorious makes one jubilant.
